# =============================================================================
# 8D. CHARTS  --  money made vs threshold, and vs trigger-day count (apples-to-apples
#     against Section 7's calendar-cadence points at comparable trade frequency)
# =============================================================================
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 5.2))

# (1) CumNet vs percentile threshold
ax = axes[0]
ax.plot(vol_df["percentile"], vol_df["CumNet"]/1e6, "o-", color="#c0392b", lw=1.8)
ax.axhline(_sta_net/1e6, color="k", ls="--", lw=1.0, label=f"Static  ${_sta_net/1e6:.1f}M")
try:
    _p0 = scen_df.loc[scen_df["scenario"].str.contains("No savings"), "CumNet"].iloc[0]
    ax.axhline(_p0/1e6, color="#2980b9", ls=":", lw=1.2, label=f"Daily calendar  ${_p0/1e6:.1f}M")
    _p2w = scen_df.loc[scen_df["scenario"] == "P2-B weekly (5d)", "CumNet"].iloc[0]
    ax.axhline(_p2w/1e6, color="#27ae60", ls=":", lw=1.2, label=f"Weekly calendar  ${_p2w/1e6:.1f}M")
except Exception:
    pass   # Section 7 not run in this session -- skip reference lines
ax.set_xlabel("Volatility trigger percentile threshold")
ax.set_ylabel("Cumulative net statutory income ($M)")
ax.set_title("Money made vs volatility threshold")
ax.legend(fontsize=8); ax.grid(alpha=0.3)

# (2) CumNet vs trigger-day count (frequency) -- the apples-to-apples view
ax2 = axes[1]
ax2.plot(vol_df["trigger_days"], vol_df["CumNet"]/1e6, "o-", color="#8e44ad", lw=1.8,
         label="Volatility-triggered")
for _, r in vol_df.iterrows():
    ax2.annotate(f"p{int(r['percentile'])}", (r["trigger_days"], r["CumNet"]/1e6),
                 fontsize=7, textcoords="offset points", xytext=(4, 4))
try:
    ax2.scatter([nD], [_p0/1e6], color="#2980b9", marker="s", s=50, label="Daily calendar (498d)", zorder=5)
    _wk_days = int((scen_df.loc[scen_df["scenario"]=="P2-B weekly (5d)"].index.size and nD/5) or 0)
    ax2.scatter([_wk_days], [_p2w/1e6], color="#27ae60", marker="s", s=50, label="Weekly calendar (~100d)", zorder=5)
except Exception:
    pass
ax2.set_xlabel("Number of trigger (trade) days over the 498-day backtest")
ax2.set_ylabel("Cumulative net ($M)")
ax2.set_title("Money made vs trading frequency\n(informed timing vs blind calendar cadence)")
ax2.legend(fontsize=8); ax2.grid(alpha=0.3)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig("fig_vol_trigger_sweep.png", dpi=100)
plt.show()

Saved: fig_vol_trigger_sweep.png

Reading¶

  • Threshold vs money made (left panel). Lower percentile thresholds trigger more often (more days count as "volatile enough to trade"), converging toward the daily-calendar result as the threshold approaches p50; higher thresholds trigger rarely and converge toward the static buy-and-hold result as the threshold approaches p95+.
  • Frequency vs money made (right panel). This is the fair comparison: at the same number of trade days, does timing those trades around volatility spikes (informed) beat spacing them evenly on a calendar (blind)? If the purple curve sits above the blue/green calendar markers at a comparable trade-day count, volatility-triggered reoptimization is capturing value calendar cadence misses — trading precisely when the book-yield surface is moving, not on an arbitrary fixed schedule. If it sits at or below, the calendar cadence is already capturing the diminishing-returns curve efficiently and the timing signal adds little beyond what a sufficiently frequent fixed cadence already achieves.
  • Use vol_df for the exact per-threshold figures (CumNet, trigger_days, adv_vs_static).

Section 8E — Window sensitivity: 7d vs 21d "current vol", 21d vs 1yr "baseline"¶

Section 8A-D fixed the signal at 21-day current vol vs its own trailing 252-day (1yr) baseline. That is one point in a 2D design space: how fast the "current volatility" measure is (short_window), and how long a history it is judged against (lookback_window). This section holds the percentile-threshold sweep fixed and instead varies the window pair itself, to see whether the choice of windows — not just the threshold — materially changes how much money the trigger makes:

Config short_window lookback_window Question it answers
7d vs 21d 7 trading days 21 trading days Does a fast vol reading, judged against just the last month, catch anything real or mostly noise?
7d vs 1yr 7 trading days 252 trading days Does a fast vol reading judged against a full year of context behave differently from judging it against only the last month?
21d vs 1yr 21 trading days 252 trading days The Section 8A-D baseline, included here for a direct side-by-side.

Each config is swept over the same percentile grid as before, so the three lines are directly comparable on both axes (threshold and money made).

In [32]:
# =============================================================================
# 8E-1. GENERALIZED SIGNAL + TRIGGER  --  parameterized short_window / lookback_window
# =============================================================================
def compute_sigma(short_window: int) -> np.ndarray:
    # Rolling std (ddof=1, bps) of the cross-sectional median book yield, any window.
    s = np.full(nD, np.nan)
    for d in range(short_window - 1, nD):
        window = _med_yield[d - short_window + 1 : d + 1]
        if np.isfinite(window).all():
            s[d] = float(np.std(window, ddof=1)) * 1e4
    return s


def trigger_days_generic(sigma_series: np.ndarray, percentile: float, lookback_window: int,
                          min_lookback: int = 10) -> np.ndarray:
    # Same self-calibrating, no-look-ahead trigger rule as trigger_days(), generalized
    # to an arbitrary lookback window (so a 21-day baseline can be tested, not just 252).
    trig = np.zeros(nD, dtype=bool)
    trig[0] = True
    for d in range(1, nD):
        if not np.isfinite(sigma_series[d]):
            trig[d] = True
            continue
        lo = max(0, d - lookback_window)
        trailing = sigma_series[lo:d][np.isfinite(sigma_series[lo:d])]
        if len(trailing) < min_lookback:
            trig[d] = True
            continue
        threshold = float(np.percentile(trailing, percentile))
        trig[d] = bool(sigma_series[d] > threshold)
    return trig


WINDOW_CONFIGS = [
    ("7d vs 21d",  7,  21),
    ("7d vs 1yr",  7,  252),
    ("21d vs 1yr", 21, 252),   # same as Section 8A-D's sigma/trigger_days, recomputed here for a clean side-by-side
]
WINDOW_PERCENTILES = [50, 60, 70, 75, 80, 90]

_sigma_cache = {sw: compute_sigma(sw) for sw in {7, 21}}
print("Signal windows computed:",
      {sw: f"{np.isfinite(s).sum()}/{nD} obs" for sw, s in _sigma_cache.items()})

Signal windows computed: {21: '478/498 obs', 7: '492/498 obs'}
In [33]:
# =============================================================================
# 8E-2. SWEEP  --  window config x percentile threshold
# =============================================================================
import time as _time8e

_win_rows, _t0 = [], _time8e.time()
for label, short_w, lookback_w in WINDOW_CONFIGS:
    sig = _sigma_cache[short_w]
    for pctl in WINDOW_PERCENTILES:
        trig = trigger_days_generic(sig, pctl, lookback_w)
        df   = run_daily_vol(trig, params=_P_vol)
        cum_net    = float(df["Net"].sum())
        trade_days = int((df["n_trades"] > 0).sum())
        row = dict(
            config          = label,
            short_window    = short_w,
            lookback_window = lookback_w,
            percentile      = pctl,
            CumNet          = cum_net,
            trigger_days    = int(trig.sum()),
            trade_days      = trade_days,
            NII             = float(df["NII"].sum()),
            Turnover        = float(df["Turnover"].sum()),
            IMR_realized    = float(df["realized_gain"].sum()),
            adv_vs_static   = cum_net - _sta_net,
        )
        row["adv_%"] = (row["adv_vs_static"] / abs(_sta_net) * 100) if abs(_sta_net) > 1 else float("nan")
        _win_rows.append(row)
        print(f"  {label:10s} p{pctl:2d}  ->  {trig.sum():3d} trigger days  "
              f"CumNet ${cum_net/1e6:6.2f}M  (vs static {row['adv_%']:+5.1f}%)")

print(f"\nAll {len(_win_rows)} runs done in {_time8e.time()-_t0:.0f}s")

window_df = pd.DataFrame(_win_rows)
print("\nBest threshold per window config:")
display(
    window_df.loc[window_df.groupby("config")["CumNet"].idxmax()]
    [["config", "percentile", "trigger_days", "CumNet", "adv_%"]]
    .sort_values("CumNet", ascending=False).reset_index(drop=True)
)

All 18 runs done in 665s

Best threshold per window config:
config percentile trigger_days CumNet adv_%
0 7d vs 21d 50 249 3.281025e+07 30.034010
1 7d vs 1yr 50 194 3.267215e+07 29.486664
2 21d vs 1yr 50 194 3.164515e+07 25.416466
In [34]:
# =============================================================================
# 8E-3. CHARTS  --  money made vs threshold and vs trigger frequency, one line per window config
# =============================================================================
_wcol = {"7d vs 21d": "#e67e22", "7d vs 1yr": "#2980b9", "21d vs 1yr": "#8e44ad"}

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 5.2))

ax = axes[0]
for label in window_df["config"].unique():
    sub = window_df[window_df["config"] == label].sort_values("percentile")
    ax.plot(sub["percentile"], sub["CumNet"]/1e6, "o-", color=_wcol[label], lw=1.8, label=label)
ax.axhline(_sta_net/1e6, color="k", ls="--", lw=1.0, label=f"Static  ${_sta_net/1e6:.1f}M")
ax.set_xlabel("Percentile threshold"); ax.set_ylabel("Cumulative net ($M)")
ax.set_title("Money made vs threshold, by window config")
ax.legend(fontsize=8); ax.grid(alpha=0.3)

ax2 = axes[1]
for label in window_df["config"].unique():
    sub = window_df[window_df["config"] == label].sort_values("trigger_days")
    ax2.plot(sub["trigger_days"], sub["CumNet"]/1e6, "o-", color=_wcol[label], lw=1.8, label=label)
ax2.set_xlabel("Number of trigger days"); ax2.set_ylabel("Cumulative net ($M)")
ax2.set_title("Money made vs trading frequency, by window config")
ax2.legend(fontsize=8); ax2.grid(alpha=0.3)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig("fig_vol_window_sensitivity.png", dpi=100)
plt.show()
print("Saved: fig_vol_window_sensitivity.png")

Saved: fig_vol_window_sensitivity.png

Reading¶

  • If the three lines sit close together at a given trigger-day count, the trigger's performance is driven mainly by how often it fires, not by which window measured volatility — i.e. the specific 7d/21d/1yr choice doesn't matter much once frequency is controlled for.
  • If 7d vs 21d clearly separates from the other two, a fast signal judged against only a month of context is picking up (or missing) something a full-year baseline wouldn't — worth checking whether it's chasing short-lived noise (self-referential threshold recalibrates too fast) rather than genuine regime shifts.
  • If 21d vs 1yr (the Section 8A-D default) dominates, the current design choice is justified; if one of the 7-day configs dominates at a comparable trigger-day count, that's evidence the signal should be sped up.
  • window_df has the full per-config, per-threshold detail for further slicing.
